title: Theorem H for frozen pyrochlore ice: proofs on the cells with a coprime pair of extents and on the cells with two chains in every pair of planes, a reduction to Theorem U alone on every cell, and the cubic cells of side one to eight
summary: Theorem H says that a frozen state of pyrochlore spin ice with a hexagon of odd curl has a dipole axis that is empty or carries one sign only. With Theorem P and Lemma A it gives the periodicity of frozen zero-flux states on every cell whose extents are all at least two. The note proves Theorem H by hand on two infinite families of cells, reduces it on every cell to one statement, Theorem U (an odd frozen state has no unoriented hole), and certifies Theorem U by DRAT proofs on the cubic cells of side four to eight and on four cells that are not cubic. Theorem U is open on the cubic cells of side nine and more. The note also records every route to Theorem U that computation has closed.

claims.label: The model (first section; Holes, cages and rods)
claims.statement: A cell $(a, b, c)$ of pyrochlore ice is the torus of quarter-cube coordinates modulo $(4a, 4b, 4c)$; its vertices are the sublattice A (even coordinates with sum $0 \bmod 4$) and B $=$ A $+ (1,1,1)$; each vertex carries four bonds in the directions $d_0, \dots, d_3$; an ice state gives every bond a direction with two in and two out at every vertex; the dipole moment of a vertex is the sum of its outgoing bond directions and its type is the axis of that moment; a hexagon is the closed walk of six bonds round an octahedral hole determined by two of the four directions; a state is frozen when no hexagon circulates, and (T2) is the matching condition that expresses this in the types; a hexagon's curl is odd or even; an odd state has an odd hexagon; the rods of a hole are the two vertices on its axis with the hole's axis as type, its bridgeheads the four vertices beside them, and a hole is oriented when one rod points towards it and one away.
claims.status_detail: Definitions. Checked for consistency with the simulation code by several independent models, most recently h730_lib (agent pacheck) and h750_model (agent p1check), which agree on the hexagon sets of four cells.

checked_by: Claude Opus 5 (agents pacheck, p1check): independent models from the definitions

claims.label: Theorem H
claims.statement: In a frozen state with a hexagon of odd curl, some axis is empty (no vertex has that type) or one-way (every vertex of that type has the same sign of moment).
claims.status_detail: Proved on the cells with a coprime pair of extents (Theorem 14), on the cells with two chains in every pair of planes (Theorem 23), and by certificate on the cubic cells of side one to eight and on four cells that are not cubic with their divisors (Theorems 2 and 24). Open elsewhere, where it follows from Theorem U by Theorem 1.

scope.cells: every cell; open on the cells with no coprime pair and more than two chains in every pair of planes that are not covered by a certificate, the cubic cells of side nine and more among them

claims.notes: The target statement of the note. Its standing by kind of cell is the table in the note's first section.

claims.label: Theorem U
claims.statement: In an odd frozen state every octahedral hole is oriented: one of its rods points towards it and the other away. Equivalent forms: an odd state has no charged hole; two consecutive vertices of type $k$ on a $k$-line have the same sign; a state with an unoriented cage has even curl; and the working form (V), that in a state with the four vertices of Theorem U′ the sublattice of the bridgeheads has no vertex of the rods' type.
claims.status_detail: Proved on the cells with a coprime pair of extents and on the cells with two chains in every pair of planes; proved for the holes of one axis when the two transverse extents are coprime (Theorem 10) or have greatest common divisor two with the rod axis of odd extent (Theorem 11); certified on the cubic cells of side four to eight and on (3,3,9), (4,4,8), (3,3,12), (6,6,9). Open on every other cell. A whole-torus search for a counterexample on the six cheapest open cells on 2026-10-01 found none, with no near miss.

scope.cells: open on cells with no coprime pair of extents and more than two chains in every pair of planes, beyond those certified

claims.notes: The one open statement between the record and Theorem H on every cell, and so between the record and the periodicity of frozen zero-flux states. Everything known about it is in the note's section "Theorem U", items 1 to 9, including the routes computation has closed; see the negative-result claims of this manifest.

claims.label: Theorem 1 (the reduction), form of 30 September 2026, with Lemmas 22 to 25
claims.statement: On every cell, Theorem U implies Theorem H.
claims.status_detail: Written argument: with every hole oriented, Theorem 6 makes the line count of a two-way type a function of one transverse coordinate on each sublattice, Theorem 3 makes the two sublattices share that coordinate, Theorem 15 kills one profile per two-way axis so that with three two-way axes some axis has a constant line count on both sublattices, and the diagonal law along the connected graph of lines makes that axis one-way. Re-derived by the main loop, then read by an independent checker with its own programs (agent check10), which confirmed it with five corrections of wording and no gap; its one prediction about odd states tested on the corpus with no exception.

claims.label: Lemma 21 (a state repeated periodically)
claims.statement: A frozen state of the cell $(a, b, c)$, repeated periodically, is a frozen state of the cell $(k_1 a, k_2 b, k_3 c)$ for any positive integers $k_1, k_2, k_3$; it has an odd hexagon exactly when the original has, and the same set of moments. So Theorem H on the larger cell implies Theorem H on the smaller.
claims.status_detail: Written by the main session and tested exactly on 765 repeated states; on 2026-10-01 read by an independent checker (agent pacheck) with its own code on eight pairs of cells with unequal multipliers, 0 violations; the direction Theorem 24 uses confirmed sound.

claims.status_detail: Rests on Theorem 12 (a statement about the types of one sublattice) and Theorem M′; on cells with two coprime pairs sharing an extent, on Theorem 13 alone. Read by an independent checker (agent check7) with its own programs; no gap.

claims.label: Theorem 10 (the coprime case of (V))
claims.statement: On a cell $(a, b, c)$ with $\gcd(b, c) = 1$, a frozen state with an unoriented hole whose rods lie along $x$ has even curl; so in an odd state every hole with rods along $x$ is oriented.
claims.status_detail: A linear argument through the parametrisation (C), once round the circle of the rod axis. Its identity verified in exact arithmetic on thirty-five cells by the author and by an independent checker, which also read the proof.

scope.cells: every cell with gcd(b, c) = 1, for holes with rods along x

claims.label: Theorem 11 (greatest common divisor two, odd length)
claims.statement: On a cell $(a, b, c)$ with $\gcd(b, c) = 2$ and $a$ odd, a frozen state with an unoriented hole whose rods lie along $x$ has even curl.
claims.status_detail: Needs integrality through a parity count on the halves of a plane; the parity of $a$ enters. Its identity verified in exact arithmetic on thirty-three cells by two implementations; read by an independent checker.

scope.cells: gcd(b, c) = 2 and a odd, for holes with rods along x

claims.notes: With $a$ even the vertex $P$ of the proof does not exist and the real relaxation has solutions; integrality is needed and no replacement for the parity count is known. Theorems 10 and 11 give no case of Theorem H that needed them.

Certified on the cubic cells of side 4, 5 and 6 by DRAT proofs checked by drat-trim: 16, 16 and 4 formulas (at side six the sixteen hypotheses form one orbit of the formula's symmetries), each with a satisfiable control whose witness was decoded and checked.

claims.label: No weighted sum of laws proves (V) at $g \geq 2$ (Theorem U section, items 3 to 5)

claims.label: Statement R, a monodromy in the weights, and the heights are not a route to (V) (Theorem U section, item 9)
claims.statement: Statement R assumed on the whole rod line shortens the reach of (V) from $2g + 1$ to $2g - 1$, and the single literal that the third rod position has the rods' type gives the same; (V) given R is false on both cut cylinders; on the grid of the bridgeheads of every cubic cell the parametrisation (C) is onto, so the real relaxation says nothing about the type set of a grid and the separability lemma has no product to act on; the weights of (C) seen along the rod axis return after $\mathrm{lcm}(\gcd(a, c), \gcd(a, b))$ cubes, which is 4 on $(12, 8, 8)$ where (V) needs 15 grids; the $g$ of the reach law is the modulus of the labels $y - z$, $y + z$ of the chains of the rod axis on the grids normal to it. Any proof of Theorem U must be integral from the first line. The branch certificates of the box lemma split into local ones, identical across $b$, and global ones that span the closed circle and grow, with no rule found.

claims.label: The kink counts per chain class: the wave equation and one defect per axis (Theorem U section, item 10)
claims.statement: On a grid normal to the rod axis, with $k[n][v]$ the number of vertices of the rods' type in the class of value $v$ (the trace of one chain of that axis), every real solution of (T2) satisfies the wave equation $k[n+2][v] + k[n-2][v] = k[n][v+2] + k[n][v-2]$ (law C summed over the holes of a class), whose solutions are two sheets travelling one class per cube in opposite senses; and on the torus every chain of an axis has the same defect, the difference of its kink counts on its two grids, because the defect obeys a smoothing recurrence along the rod axis whose non-constant modes die round the circle.
claims.status_detail: Hand proofs by one agent with no second reader; the wave equation and the summed law verified to lie in the row space of the window's equations and exact on 488 enumerated models on four cells; the single defect checked on 5,119 frozen states of five cells on all three axes; the main loop re-ran the corpus check and two solver rows.

claims.label: The kink counts per class cannot close (V) (Theorem U section, item 10)
claims.statement: By solver on four cells with controls, the pattern of (V) makes the defect one constant on every chain of a three-grid window, non-negative on $[-3, 2g - 2]$, and with the negation zero on $[-3, 2g - 1]$ and not before, so given the pattern on the torus (V) is equivalent to a positive defect, with the same reach $2g + 1$. Two parallel unit sheets of one sense through the two rods with defect zero satisfy the wave equation, the summed law $P^k$, Lemma 6, the bounds, the pins of the pattern and the negation round the whole torus of each cell, and every enumerated solution short of the threshold extends by the wave equation round the rod axis within the bounds. The obstruction lies in which positions inside a class are kinked, not in how many.
claims.status_detail: Solver with controls (23 batches, four cells) and an exact witness (h767) on four cells; the main loop re-ran the witness on two cells and the defect queries on one window.

claims.label: The weights of (C) are rarely integral (correction of 30 September 2026)
claims.statement: The gauge orbit of the chain weights contains an integer vector on 19 of the 637 odd frozen states of the cubic cell of side three, 20 of the 720 of side four, and none of 60 sampled solutions of the type model, with least denominators from 27 to 96 otherwise. The report of 10 September that says the weights can be taken integral on every state examined had examined those 19, and its height results are proved for integral weights only.

claims.label: Periodicity of frozen zero-flux states (first section, with Theorem P and Lemma A of the earlier note)
claims.statement: On every cell whose extents are all at least two, Theorem H implies that every frozen zero-flux state is invariant under a nonzero translation: if an axis is empty Lemma A gives the translation; otherwise zero flux makes every axis two-way, so the state has even curl by Theorem H, and Theorem P gives a one-cube period. So periodicity holds on the cubic cells of side one to eight (side one by direct computation), on the cells with a coprime pair of extents all at least two, on the cells with two chains in every pair of planes, and on the cells certified on 2026-10-01 with their divisors.
claims.status_detail: The chain Lemma L, Lemma A, Theorem P (through its first step P1) and Lemma 21 was read on 2026-10-01 by two independent checkers with their own programs (agents pacheck, p1check); only Lemma C (even curl implies frozen) of the earlier record has had no checker. The hypothesis on the extents was missing from the note's first draft and is needed: see claim thin-cells-aperiodic.

scope.cells: every cell with all extents at least two on which Theorem H holds

claims.label: Frozen zero-flux states with no translation symmetry on thin cells

This refutes the periodicity conclusion on thin cells and shows that Theorem P's hypothesis that every extent is at least two cannot be dropped.
